entry.title: grave of Ethel Preston (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that the grave of Ethel Preston in Leeds, England, has a life-sized statue of her (pictured) stood in front of black marble doors, left ajar?

entry.title: Moses sees Rabbi Akiva (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that meetings between Biblical and post-Biblical characters, such as when Moses sees Rabbi Akiva teach and be martyred, are rare in Talmudic stories?

entry.title: Marie-Thérèse Eyquem (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that Marie-Thérèse Eyquem served in the government of Vichy France, and was later appointed a national secretary of the French Socialist Party?

entry.title: An Amorous History of the Silver Screen (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that An Amorous History of the Silver Screen, an exploration of more than four decades of film in China, argues that cinema is a "modern folk tale"?

entry.title: Tema "Sacher" (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that a critic called Benjamin Britten's Tema "Sacher" a "truncated and barely coherent page [of music]" and "a pathetic fragment"?

entry.title: Beechcraft BQM-126 (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that the 1980s Beechcraft BQM-126 target drone could be launched from aircraft based on aircraft carriers?

entry.title: Mary Chalmers (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that children's author Mary Chalmers owned ten cats and a Pomeranian dog, whose poses helped her draw illustrations for her books?

entry.title: 1917 Moscow District Duma elections (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that in the 1917 Moscow District Duma elections, the Bolshevik Party won 97 percent of the votes of the soldiers at the heavy artillery workshops?

entry.title: Flora Hommel (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that Flora Hommel, after being afraid of giving birth to her own child, went on to teach the Lamaze technique to more than 17,000 couples?
